title: Митинги в Грузии переросли в неконтролируемые беспорядки: пострадали уже более 20 полицейских
content: Massive riots erupted in Tbilisi, Georgia, on October 4, 2025, amid local elections, escalating into uncontrollable violence. According to the Georgian Ministry of Health, 6 protesters and 21 police officers were injured during clashes. The injured were transported to medical facilities, and the ministry confirmed there were no fatalities. In the evening, a group of individuals breached metal barriers at the presidential residence on Atkhoneli Street. Security forces, including police and special units, repelled the crowd using water cannons and pepper spray. The incident marks a significant escalation in political unrest ahead of the elections.

title: Number of people detained in connection with riots in Tbilisi rises to 45
content: The number of people detained in connection with the October 4 riots in Tbilisi, Georgia, has risen to 45, according to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Georgia, as reported by APA's local bureau. The detainees include both organizers and participants of a protest that turned violent. The protest, which occurred on October 4 during municipal elections, aimed at a peaceful revolution and involved an attempt by demonstrators to storm the Presidential Palace. Clashes between police and protesters resulted in injuries on both sides. The latest detainee is a person born in 1987.

title: 11 arrested after clashes in Exarchia district
content: Eleven individuals were arrested following clashes between self-styled anarchists and police in Athens’ Exarchia district during the early hours of Saturday, according to authorities. The confrontation occurred when a group attacked a riot police unit stationed outside the headquarters of the opposition PASOK party on Harilaou Trikoupi Street. Police responded with tear gas, and the unrest lasted approximately 30 minutes, causing disruption in the neighborhood. The motive behind the attack remains unclear.

title: Güney Kıbrıs'ta 19 yılda 462 ırkçı aaldırı: 2023 ve 2024 zirvede
content: According to 'Simerini gazetesi', based on 'polisin resmi verilerine dayanarak', 462 racist attacks were recorded in Southern Cyprus between 2005 and 2024, involving 719 perpetrators and affecting 613 victims. The majority of both victims and perpetrators were Greek Cypriots. The highest number of incidents occurred in 2023 with 57 attacks, followed closely by 54 in 2024. The attacks were primarily motivated by ethnic origin, skin colour and sexual orientation.

title: تصاعد حدة الاحتجاجات وتحولها إلى أعمال تخريبية في إنزكان وبني ملال واشتوكة - هبة بريس
content: Protests in multiple Moroccan cities, including Inzkan, Beni Mellal, and the commune of Aït Ammira in the province of Chichaoua, escalated into violent confrontations on Tuesday, September 30, 2025. The unrest included arson and destruction of vehicles—some belonging to security forces—direct clashes between protesters and police and royal gendarmerie, stone-throwing, and fires. Video footage circulated online showed burned cars in Aït Ammira, reflecting rising public anger. The demonstrations, now in their fourth consecutive day, have seen increased mobilization among youth, particularly members of 'Generation Z,' demanding deep political, economic, and social reforms. The protest movement expanded to new cities such as Inzkan and Beni Mellal, joining major protest hubs like Fes, Tangier, Rabat, Tétouan, and Casablanca. The Presidency of the Government’s majority coalition, following a morning meeting, expressed understanding of social demands and pledged a 'positive and responsible' response through dialogue within public institutions and spaces, aiming to find practical, implementable solutions that serve national and citizen interests. Social media continues to drive mobilization, with calls for protests in over ten cities, while judicial monitoring is ongoing for several detainees linked to the events, which began on Saturday, September 26, 2025.

title: Émeutes du mercredi : 354 blessés, 3 morts et forte implication de...
content: The Ministry of the Interior announced the aftermath of violent riots that shook the Kingdom during the night of Wednesday, October 1, 2025. The unrest, following the GenZ movement, resulted in 3 deaths, 354 injuries, and the destruction of 80 public buildings. According to the ministry, 70% of those involved were minors, with many of the rioters being underage. Violent acts included stone-throwing, use of bladed weapons, and assaults on public buildings and security posts. In Leqliaa, in the province of Inzegane Ait-Melloul, a group of masked individuals attempted to attack a gendarmerie unit to seize service weapons and ammunition, prompting security forces to respond with live rounds in self-defense, resulting in three fatalities. Among the injured, 326 were members of law enforcement. A total of 271 police vehicles and 175 civilian cars were set on fire. The authorities have placed adult suspects under custody and applied precautionary measures to minors in accordance with legal rights. The Ministry emphasized that all necessary measures will be taken firmly and without compromise against those involved. Security forces will continue operations in line with constitutional duties and legal mandates to restore order and apprehend all participants in the riots.

title: Массовые протесты в Грузии: что известно на 5 октября
content: On October 4, 2025, mass protests occurred in Tbilisi, Georgia, during municipal elections, resulting in six protesters and 21 police officers being injured, one of whom is in critical condition. Georgian authorities reported that five individuals were arrested and accused of organizing the protests, inciting violent change to the constitutional order, overthrowing the government, and participating in group violence, with potential sentences of up to nine years in prison. Among the accused is Paata Burculadze, founder of the opposition movement 'Prospect Rustaveli', an opera singer, and People's Artist of the Georgian SSR, who was reportedly among the first to call for a storming of the presidential palace and was injured by a pepper spray canister during the dispersal of demonstrators. He was hospitalized, where security forces later arrived. Other detained individuals include Murtaz Zodelava and Irakli Nadiradze from the 'National Movement', Paata Mandjgaladze from 'Strategy Agmashenebeli', and Colonel Lasha Beridze—all members of the organizing committee for the October 4 rally. According to the Ministry of Health of Georgia, the injuries occurred during violent clashes. Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze stated that all participants were involved in an attempted coup, claiming they should be expected to carry out further actions in the coming days, and accused foreign intelligence agencies and the EU ambassador of orchestrating the unrest. Municipal elections were held in 64 municipalities, including five self-governing cities: Tbilisi, Kutaisi, Batumi, Poti, and Rustavi. The vote count is ongoing, and Kobakhidze claimed the ruling party 'Georgian Dream' received over 70% of the votes in all municipalities.

title: Gürcistan'da protestoda arbede! 21 polis ve 6 gösterici yaralandı
content: In Tbilisi, Georgia, a protest demonstration on October 4, 2024, resulted in clashes between police and demonstrators, leaving 21 police officers and 6 protesters injured, according to a statement from the Ministry of Labour, Health and Social Protection of Georgia. Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze accused protesters of attempting a coup against the government, claiming they sought to seize the Presidential Palace and that their efforts failed. He warned that anyone using illegal means to overthrow the government would face a 'severe response,' stating, 'The law will be very strict.' Several opposition parties, including the United National Movement, rejected the results of the October 4 local elections and declared they would not recognize the 2024 parliamentary and presidential elections. Opera singer Paata Burçuladze, a protest organizer, declared during a speech at Freedom Square that the government was no longer legitimate since October 4. He called for top government officials to be handed over to justice. Murtaz Zodelava, a United National Movement representative, urged demonstrators to 'seize the Presidential Palace,' prompting a group to attempt forced entry, leading to clashes with police. Protesters threw stones and bottles, prompting police special forces to respond with tear gas. Police also used high-pressure water cannons to disperse demonstrators blocking barriers. Further clashes occurred at Orbeliani Square, where police and protesters confronted each other during the ongoing protest.

title: На фоне муниципальных выборов в Тбилиси прошли массовые беспорядки
content: Mass riots erupted in Tbilisi, Georgia, on October 4, 2025, amid municipal elections held across 64 municipalities, including five self-governing cities: Tbilisi, Batumi, Kutaisi, Rustavi, and Poti. The elections involved 12 political parties, with opposition parties boycotting the vote. The Central Election Commission declared that the ruling party, 'Georgian Dream,' won in all 64 municipalities, triggering widespread protests. Demonstrators, including students from Tbilisi State University, marched on Rustaveli Avenue, set fires in the city center, and breached the presidential residence, according to TV Pirveli. Police responded with water cannons, and the Ministry of Internal Affairs stated the protests had gone beyond legal limits. At least 27 people were injured—six protesters and 21 police officers—with one officer in critical condition. Thirty others received on-site medical aid. Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze blamed the European Union's ambassador and accused foreign intelligence agencies of orchestrating the unrest, claiming all responsible would face 'strict consequences.' The Ministry of Internal Affairs opened a criminal case under four articles, including incitement to overthrow the constitutional order. On October 5, five organizers were detained: Murat Zodelav (former chief prosecutor and member of 'United National Movement'), Irakli Nadiradze, opera singer and protest leader Paata Burculadze, party leader Paata Mandjgaladze, and retired colonel and former deputy chief of the General Staff Lasha Beridze. Zodelav reportedly urged protesters to move toward the Orbeliani Presidential Palace to 'take the keys.' Despite claims by opposition figures like Giorgi Lomia that protests would continue due to distrust in election results, experts such as Sergei Margulies from the Presidential Academy suggest the unrest may subside within days, noting repeated slogans and lack of radical outcomes. The final voter turnout was 40.93%. European Parliament and Georgian opposition had previously rejected results of the 2024 parliamentary elections, which were also won by 'Georgian Dream.'

title: Unrest in Georgia as protesters clash with police after ruling party wins local body polls
content: Unrest erupted in Georgia on October 5, 2025, following local elections in which the ruling Georgian Dream (GD) party claimed victory across all municipal seats in the country of 3.7 million people. The opposition, boycotting the vote, accused GD of being pro-Russian and authoritarian, and staged a massive demonstration in Tbilisi's Freedom Square, waving Georgian and EU flags. Protesters attempted to forcibly enter the presidential palace, leading to violent clashes with police who used pepper spray and water cannons. Twenty-one security personnel and six protesters were injured. Five activists, including opera singer Paata Burchuladze and two members of the United National Movement, were detained and face charges of inciting the overthrow of the government, which could result in up to nine years in prison if convicted. The tensions stem from the October 2024 parliamentary elections, which opposition groups deemed fraudulent. Since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Georgia’s relations with the West have deteriorated, culminating in the government freezing EU accession talks after the 2024 vote, triggering ongoing mass protests. Georgian Dream is led by Bidzina Ivanishvili, Georgia’s richest man and former prime minister, who denies allegations of pro-Moscow alignment.
